verbalization: Estrone sulfate is implicated in the regulation of P-glycoprotein 1 through a complex network of molecular interactions. The evidence suggests that Estrone sulfate acts as a target for a specific protein, (3R,5S,7S)-8-hydroxy-4,4,7-trimethyl-9-(2-methylbutanoyl)-3-prop-1-en-2-yltricyclo[5.3.1.01,5]undec-8-ene-10,11-dione, which in turn targets P-glycoprotein 1. This pathway implies that Estrone sulfate may influence the expression or activity of P-glycoprotein 1, potentially through direct or indirect mechanisms involving the intermediate protein. The presence of a high confidence score in the relationship between Estrone sulfate and ATP-binding cassette sub-family G member 1 further supports the notion that this intermediate protein serves as a critical mediator in the interaction between Estrone sulfate and P-glycoprotein 1. The integration of these pathways highlights the role of P-glycoprotein 1 in drug resistance and suggests that Estrone sulfate may modulate its activity, offering a potential mechanism for its pharmacological effects.
